permutationLabel: Reverse mimic: gradual onset STI epididymo-orchitis with normal Doppler
summary: 27-year-old man with 3 days of gradual right scrotal pain, dysuria, urethral discharge and fever 38.1; tender epididymis, cremasteric reflex present, Doppler normal testicular flow.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful swelling of the right side of the scrotum over 3 days
inputs.hpi: Three days of gradually increasing right scrotal pain and swelling, with burning on passing urine and a urethral discharge for a week. New partner 3 weeks ago, condoms not used. Mild fever. No vomiting.

exam.other: Genitalia: tender swollen right epididymis, normal testicular lie, cremasteric reflex present, pain eased by elevation. Urethral discharge.

imaging.name: Scrotal Doppler ultrasound
imaging.result: Enlarged hyperaemic right epididymis with increased flow; normal testicular flow bilaterally; no torsion.

inputs.socialHistory: Chef. New sexual partner 3 weeks ago.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right epididymo-orchitis (probable sexually transmitted infection)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right epididymo-orchitis, likely STI (urethritis, new partner); Doppler shows normal testicular flow.

mustNotMiss.note: Torsion stays on the differential until excluded.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE ranks epididymo-orchitis, appendicitis, inguinal hernia; torsion is not in the top 3 (symptom inference lists "torsion / epididymo-orchitis" #2). | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 5 of ios.bayes: 1. Inguinal Hernia | 2. Hydrocele | 3. Epididymo-orchitis | 4. Fournier's Gangrene | 5. Incarcerated / Strangulated Hernia
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Calibrate pane-engine urology likelihoods/priors and map the urinary chips (loin pain, dysuria, retention, haematuria, scrotal) and the "Other / general surgical" CC into PANE features, as SmartSymptomPicker chips do for symptom inference.

emergencyLevel.note: Same-day review, not an emergency, once Doppler shows normal testicular flow and onset is gradual (over-triage check).
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web: Triage "emergency_now" (score 48): fever in the text and the 38.1 °C vital plus a moderate pain score add up past the emergency threshold (45); the scrotal chip itself adds nothing.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Negation handling in triage free text; do not escalate gradual scrotal pain with normal Doppler flow.

mustExclude.note: Exploration is right when torsion cannot be excluded; here gradual onset, urethritis and normal Doppler flow make an unconditional exploration plan over-treatment.

guideline.name: IUSTI/WHO European guideline on the management of epididymo-orchitis
guideline.section: Exclude torsion (surgical exploration if in doubt); test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea (NAAT) and urine culture; likely STI: ceftriaxone plus doxycycline; enteric organisms likely: fluoroquinolone; scrotal support and analgesia; partner notification
guideline.citation: Street EJ, Justice ED, Kopa Z, et al. The 2016 European guideline on the management of epididymo-orchitis. Int J STD AIDS. 2017;28:744–749.

guideline.name: EAU/ESPU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology — acute scrotum
guideline.section: Testicular torsion is a clinical diagnosis; urgent surgical exploration; Doppler ultrasound must not delay surgery; explore when torsion cannot be excluded
guideline.citation: Radmayr C, Bogaert G, Burgu B, et al. EAU Guidelines on Paediatric Urology. EAU Guidelines Office, Arnhem; 2024 edition. Section: Acute scrotum in children.

rationale: The counterpart to torsion: gradual onset with urethritis and normal testicular flow. IUSTI 2016: STI tests, ceftriaxone plus doxycycline, partner notification.
